topStories.title: 要闻：在与 SEC Consult 漏洞实验室合作开展一项研究项目期间，以 SMTP 走私攻击闻名的 Timo Lon
topStories.originalTitle: From: anyone@icloud.com - Spoofing Arbitrary Apple iCloud Identities
topStories.fullContent:
In the course of a research project in collaboration with the SEC Consult Vulnerability Lab, Timo Longin (@timolongin) - known for SMTP smuggling - discovered two exotic email spoofing vulnerabilities in Apple iCloud's emailing infrastructure.

At the end of 2023 SMTP smuggling made a dramatic entrance, allowing email spoofing for millions of email servers worldwide. Ever wanted to send emails as admin@outlook.com while still passing SPF checks? SMTP smuggling had you covered!

However, in 2024, most SMTP implementations adapted, and released security updates for their software. Does this mean the end of SMTP smuggling? Or does this attack have more to offer?

Let's dive into a case study of Apple iCloud's SMTP parsing jungle and try to spoof emails once more!

Note: This blog post is related to SMTP Smuggling - Spoofing E-Mails Worldwide. For additional contextual and background information, we recommend reading it first.

Even though no novel techniques for traditional SMTP smuggling were discovered, a subclass of email spoofing was explored - header smuggling. Again highlighting the parsing discrepancies in SMTP implementations, header smuggling builds upon the lessons of its bigger brother SMTP smuggling. Based on a case study of Apple iCloud's emailing services, we once again reveal the dangers of trusting emails by being able to send messages from arbitrary icloud.com addresses.

First of all, let's have a short recap on SMTP smuggling. With traditional SMTP smuggling, we exploited interpretation differences of the SMTP protocol between outbound (sending) and inbound (receiving) SMTP servers. More specifically, we capitalized on the fact that lots of SMTP implementations deviated from RFCs, leading to different understandings of the so-called end-of-data sequence. Since the end-of-data sequence indicates where the message data ends, we could achieve the following between vulnerable outbound and inbound SMTP servers (figure 1).
topStories.fullTranslation:
在与 SEC Consult 漏洞实验室合作开展一项研究项目期间，以 SMTP 走私攻击闻名的 Timo Longin（@timolongin）发现了 Apple iCloud 电子邮件基础设施中的两种罕见电子邮件伪造漏洞。

2023 年年底，SMTP 走私攻击以一种戏剧性的方式登场，使全球数百万台电子邮件服务器面临电子邮件伪造风险。是否曾经想过，在通过 SPF 检查的同时，以 admin@outlook.com 的身份发送电子邮件？SMTP 走私攻击可以满足这一需求！

然而，到了 2024 年，大多数 SMTP 实现都进行了调整，并发布了软件安全更新。这是否意味着 SMTP 走私攻击就此终结？还是说，这种攻击还有更多可能性？

让我们深入研究 Apple iCloud 的 SMTP 解析丛林，并再次尝试伪造电子邮件！

注意：这篇博客文章与《SMTP 走私——在全球范围内伪造电子邮件》有关。如需了解更多上下文和背景信息，我们建议先阅读该文章。

尽管研究没有发现传统 SMTP 走私攻击的新技术，但研究人员探索了一类电子邮件伪造的子类型——标头走私。这再次凸显了 SMTP 实现中的解析差异；标头走私建立在其“前辈”SMTP 走私攻击的经验之上。基于对 Apple iCloud 电子邮件服务的案例研究，我们再次揭示了盲目信任电子邮件的危险：攻击者能够从任意 icloud.com 地址发送消息。

首先，让我们简要回顾一下 SMTP 走私攻击。在传统的 SMTP 走私攻击中，我们利用了出站（发送）SMTP 服务器与入站（接收）SMTP 服务器对 SMTP 协议的理解差异。更具体地说，我们利用了这样一个事实：大量 SMTP 实现偏离了 RFC 标准，导致它们对所谓的“数据结束序列”产生不同理解。由于数据结束序列标示了消息数据的结束位置，因此在存在漏洞的出站 SMTP 服务器与入站 SMTP 服务器之间，我们可以实现以下效果（见图 1）。
keyTakeaways: 文章称，Timo Longin（@timolongin）在与 SEC Consult Vulnerability Lab 合作开展研究期间，发现了 Apple iCloud 邮件基础设施中的两种电子邮件欺骗漏洞。
文章称，SMTP smuggling 在 2023 年底引起关注，并使针对全球数百万邮件服务器的电子邮件欺骗成为可能。

来源叙事重点：聚焦 Apple iCloud 邮件基础设施中的电子邮件身份伪造风险，强调 SMTP smuggling 与 header smuggling 所利用的不同邮件服务器解析逻辑，并以研究者声称能够从任意 icloud.com 地址发送邮件作为案例。文章同时将该发现置于 2023 年 SMTP smuggling 受到关注、2024 年相关实现陆续修复的背景中。文中“dramatic entrance”“parsing jungle”“dangers of trusting emails”等表述体现了安全研究和风险警示框架，不应视为独立验证的事实。

facts.claim: 文章称，Timo Longin（@timolongin）在与 SEC Consult Vulnerability Lab 合作开展研究期间，发现了 Apple iCloud 邮件基础设施中的两种电子邮件欺骗漏洞。
文章称，SMTP smuggling 在 2023 年底引起关注，并使针对全球数百万邮件服务器的电子邮件欺骗成为可能。
文章称，2024 年大多数 SMTP 实现进行了适配，并发布了相关安全更新。
文章称，研究没有发现传统 SMTP smuggling 的新技术，但探索了电子邮件欺骗的一个子类，即 header smuggling。
文章称，header smuggling 建立在 SMTP smuggling 的经验之上，并涉及不同 SMTP 实现之间的解析差异。
文章称，在 Apple iCloud 邮件服务的案例研究中，可以发送来自任意 icloud.com 地址的邮件。
文章解释称，传统 SMTP smuggling 利用了出站 SMTP 服务器与入站 SMTP 服务器对 SMTP 协议的不同解释，尤其是对 RFC 偏离以及邮件数据结束序列的不同理解。

topStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Google’s midrange Fitbit Edge shows off is many sides and colors in leaked images.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Terrence O'Brien

We don’t know a ton about the Fitbit Edge, but it appears to be a successor to the midrange Charge line. It had leaked previously, but we can clearly see in these images posted by Android Headlines, you can see that Google’s rumored fitness tracker sort of splits the difference between the Pixel Watch and the Fitbit Air. It has a small screen that is able to display some widgets, but clearly isn’t as expansive as a proper smartwatch.

Supposedly, this fitness-first wearable will have a seven-day battery life, as well as built-in GPS and an altimeter, making it far more capable than the minimalist Air. It will also have limited app support for things like Google Maps and YouTube Music. Beyond that, not a ton is known.

The Fitbit Charge line was last updated in 2023, so a new midrange tracker is long overdue. While we don’t have any word on price or release date yet, somewhere in the $150 to $200 range seems like a safe bet. The Air costs $99.99 and the Watch starts at $399.99, so the Edge would clearly fall somewhere in the middle. The Charge 6 currently goes for $159.95.

我们对 Fitbit Edge 目前所知不多，但它似乎是中端 Charge 产品线的继任者。此前已有相关泄露信息，而从 Android Headlines 发布的这些图片中可以清楚看到，传闻中的这款谷歌健身追踪器似乎介于 Pixel Watch 和 Fitbit Air 之间。它配备了一块小屏幕，能够显示一些小组件，但显然没有真正的智能手表那么大的显示范围。

据称，这款以健身为核心的可穿戴设备续航时间将达到七天，并内置 GPS 和高度计，因此功能远比极简的 Air 更强。它还将有限支持 Google 地图和 YouTube Music 等应用。除此之外，目前尚无太多信息。

Fitbit Charge 产品线最近一次更新是在 2023 年，因此一款新的中端追踪器早就应该推出了。虽然目前还没有价格或发布日期方面的消息，但预计售价在 150 至 200 美元之间应该比较稳妥。Air 的售价为 99.99 美元，而 Watch 的起售价为 399.99 美元，因此 Edge 显然会处于两者之间。目前 Charge 6 的售价为 159.95 美元。

topStories.title: 华尔街迎来新对手，而它就深植于这个南方州的腹地
topStories.originalTitle: Wall Street has a new rival, and it's deep in the heart of this southern state
topStories.snippet: The Texas Stock Exchange wants to challenge Wall Street's dominance as former Rep. Jeb Hensarling says Texas is America's new economic center.
topStories.fullContent:
DALLAS — Wall Street has long been the undisputed home of American finance. Now, one southern state wants a seat at the table.

The Texas Stock Exchange is at the center of an ambitious effort to transform the Lone Star State into America's next financial powerhouse, challenging the long-standing dominance of the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq while fueling the rise of what's become affectionately known as " Y'all Street ."

The Dallas-based exchange plans to provide companies with another venue to list their shares and raise capital, with supporters betting it will help establish Texas as America's next financial frontier.

ONE SOUTHERN STATE'S RISE IS MAKING IT AMERICA'S NEW 'ECONOMIC CENTER OF GRAVITY'

Former Rep. Jeb Hensarling, R-Texas, a strategic advisor and member of the Texas Stock Exchange, believes the shift is already underway.

"Texas is really becoming the economic center of gravity in America," Hensarling told Fox News Digital during an interview at the Texas Stock Exchange's headquarters.

"As New York is increasingly shoving capital out, Texas is saying, 'You're welcome here,'" he said. "We put out the welcome mat, whereas New York, capital isn't really made to feel at home, and capital wants to go where it's made to feel at home."

Hensarling argued that years of pro-business policies have helped transform Texas into more than just an attractive place to operate a company.

GOV ABBOTT EXTENDS OFF-RAMP FOR NY BILLIONAIRES FLEEING MAMDANI'S POLICIES

"Texas has been a great place to do business for decades, but increasingly it's a great place to headquarter your business," he said. "Over the last couple of legislative sessions, because of laws passed, it's a great place to incorporate your business."

"The last piece of that puzzle was the Texas Stock Exchange," Hensarling said. "It's now making Texas the best place to list your company and to go public."

BILLIONS IN TAXPAYER INCOME ARE LEAVING TWO ICONIC STATES — AS A NEW ECONOMIC MAP EMERGES

The exchange is part of a broader wave of investment flowing into Texas . In recent years, major corporations have moved their headquarters to the state, while financial giants including Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, Charles Schwab and Bank of America have expanded their Texas operations.

Supporters say those moves reflect a larger migration of businesses and capital away from traditional financial centers toward states with lower taxes and lighter regulation.

Critics, however, note that New York remains the country's dominant financial hub by a wide margin, with the world's largest stock exchange, major investment banks and deep capital markets.

THIS STATE ISN'T JUST GROWING — ITS ECONOMY IS GETTING RICHER PER RESIDENT

Whether "Y'all Street" can truly rival Wall Street remains an open question.

But with a new stock exchange, an influx of corporate headquarters and some of the nation's biggest financial firms expanding in Dallas, Texas is making its boldest bid yet to challenge Wall Street's dominance.

Hensarling believes the trajectory is clear.

"Texas is really becoming the economic center of gravity in America," he said.

达拉斯——长期以来，华尔街一直是美国金融业毋庸置疑的中心。如今，一个南方州希望在这张桌子旁占有一席之地。

得克萨斯证券交易所正处于一项雄心勃勃的行动核心，旨在将“孤星之州”转变为美国下一个金融强州。该交易所正在挑战纽约证券交易所和纳斯达克长期以来的主导地位，同时推动一个被亲切地称为“乡亲街”（Y'all Street）的金融中心崛起。

这家总部位于达拉斯的交易所计划为企业提供另一个股票上市和筹集资本的平台。支持者押注，这将有助于确立得克萨斯州作为美国下一个金融前沿的地位。

一个南方州的崛起正使其成为美国新的“经济重心”

前联邦众议员、得克萨斯州共和党人杰布·亨萨林，是得克萨斯证券交易所的战略顾问和成员。他认为，这一转变已经开始。

亨萨林在得克萨斯证券交易所总部接受福克斯新闻数字频道采访时说：“得克萨斯州确实正在成为美国的经济重心。”

他说：“随着纽约越来越把资本拒之门外，得克萨斯州则在说：‘欢迎来到这里。’我们铺开了欢迎的地毯；而在纽约，资本并没有真正感到宾至如归，而资本希望流向让它感到宾至如归的地方。”

亨萨林认为，多年来亲商的政策帮助得克萨斯州从一个有吸引力的企业经营地，转变为更具吸引力的企业总部所在地。

州长阿博特为逃离曼达尼政策的纽约亿万富翁延长“退出通道”

他说：“几十年来，得克萨斯州一直是开展商业活动的好地方，但如今越来越成为设立企业总部的好地方。过去几届立法会议期间，由于通过了相关法律，这里也成为注册企业的好地方。”

亨萨林说：“这块拼图的最后一部分就是得克萨斯证券交易所。如今，它正使得克萨斯州成为企业上市和首次公开募股的最佳地点。”

数十亿美元的纳税人收入正离开两个标志性州——一幅新的经济版图正在浮现

这家交易所是流入得克萨斯州的更广泛投资浪潮的一部分。近年来，多家大型企业将总部迁至该州；与此同时，高盛、摩根大通、嘉信理财和美国银行等金融巨头也扩大了在得克萨斯州的业务。

支持者表示，这些举措反映出一种更大范围的企业和资本迁移趋势：它们正从传统金融中心转向税负更低、监管更宽松的州。

不过，批评者指出，纽约仍以很大优势保持着美国金融中心的主导地位，拥有全球最大的证券交易所、主要投资银行以及规模深厚的资本市场。

这个州不只是正在增长——其人均经济财富也在增加

“乡亲街”能否真正与华尔街抗衡，仍是一个悬而未决的问题。

但随着一家新的证券交易所成立、企业总部不断涌入，以及美国一些最大的金融公司在达拉斯扩大业务，得克萨斯州正以前所未有的力度挑战华尔街的主导地位。

亨萨林认为，发展轨迹已经十分清晰。

他说：“得克萨斯州确实正在成为美国的经济重心。”

topStories.fullContent: Crude oil prices fell in early trading, though Brent remained above $100, after a report from Kpler revealed that flows out of the Strait of Hormuz are now above pre-war levels. The same firm made headlines last week after saying tanker traffic via Hormuz was close to pre-war levels, despite Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and Iranian attacks on tankers in Hormuz. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $101.20 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate at $89.73 per barrel. Brent was actually up from Friday in absolute terms, and so was WTI, suggesting that some in the trading world, at least, were waiting for harder evidence of improving flows. According to what Reuters called “provisional data” from Kpler, oil flows out of Hormuz ranged between 19.5 million barrels daily and 22.5 million barrels daily between September 27 and September 29. This is about double the daily flows from a month earlier, and comes despite reports of substantial disruption in Saudi energy infrastructure. The data also comes after weeks of reports, citing Kpler data again, that daily flows via Hormuz remained below the ten-day moving average, sparking doubts among some energy market commentators. The doubts were reinforced by reports about Iranian attacks on tankers in Hormuz, although some have dismissed the attacks as a factor in prices. Per the Kpler provisional data, LNG flows out of Hormuz are also at pre-war levels, which is an interesting development given that QatarEnergy is still in force majeure mode on exports, although reports have emerged saying it was looking to buy some LNG cargoes to service some of its long-term contracts. Even with these emergency purchases, it is unlikely that flows out of the world’s third-largest LNG exporters are back to pre-war levels amid a force majeure. By Irina Slav for Oilprice.com
topStories.fullTranslation: 由于克普勒（Kpler）的一份报告显示，霍尔木兹海峡的原油外运量目前已超过战前水平，原油价格在早盘交易中下跌，但布伦特原油价格仍高于每桶100美元。上周，这家公司曾因表示经由霍尔木兹海峡的油轮通行量已接近战前水平而成为新闻焦点，尽管胡塞武装袭击了沙特能源基础设施，伊朗也袭击了霍尔木兹海峡的油轮。截至发稿时，布伦特原油报每桶101.20美元，西得克萨斯中质原油报每桶89.73美元。按绝对价格计算，布伦特原油实际上较周五有所上涨，西得克萨斯中质原油也是如此，这表明至少交易界的部分人士仍在等待有关流量改善的更有力证据。据路透社所称的克普勒“临时数据”，9月27日至9月29日期间，经霍尔木兹海峡外运的石油日流量介于1,950万桶和2,250万桶之间。这一水平约为一个月前日流量的两倍，尽管有报道称沙特能源基础设施遭到了大规模破坏。该数据发布之际，此前数周的报道也一直援引克普勒数据称，经霍尔木兹海峡的日流量仍低于10日移动平均值，引发了一些能源市场评论人士的怀疑。有关伊朗袭击霍尔木兹海峡油轮的报道进一步加深了这些疑虑，不过一些人认为这些袭击并不是影响油价的因素。根据克普勒的临时数据，霍尔木兹海峡的液化天然气（LNG）外运量也已达到战前水平。鉴于卡塔尔能源公司目前仍因出口问题处于不可抗力状态，这一进展颇为引人关注；不过，有报道称该公司正在寻求购买一些液化天然气现货船货，以履行部分长期合同。即便进行了这些应急采购，在处于不可抗力状态的情况下，全球第三大液化天然气出口国的外运量恢复到战前水平也不太可能。伊琳娜·斯拉夫为Oilprice.com撰写

topStories.originalTitle: Google froze its open source bug bounty program due to a ‘significant rise’ in AI submissions
topStories.snippet: AI slop seems to be overwhelming bug bounty programs.
topStories.fullContent:
Blaming a “significant rise” in AI submissions, Google has paused its open source bug bounty program until next year.

Last year, TechCrunch reported that cybersecurity experts were warning of that AI slop posed a serious risk to bug bounty programs. Looks like that’s the issue confronting Google’s Open Source Software Vulnerability Rewards Program, where researchers were rewarded for finding vulnerabilities in the company’s open source software.

In posts on X and the program website, Google said the bug bounty program was paused as of October 1, with a promise to provide “an update” in the first quarter of 2027. According to Tom’s Hardware, Google engineers and open source maintainers were overwhelmed by reports that were invalid or contained hallucinations.

“This pause is due to a significant rise in automated submissions, the vast majority of which are not valid,” the company said.

In the meantime, participants are encouraged to consider Google’s other bug bounty programs.

topStories.fullContent:

See All Entertainment

If Trent Reznor studied musical theater instead of computer engineering NIN might have sounded like Prick.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Terrence O'Brien

While deep in the recording process for The Downward Spiral, Trent Reznor lent some of his production talents to old friend Kevin McMahon, from the new wave band Lucky Pierre (which Reznor was briefly a member of). While Reznor is only credited as the producer on four tracks off Prick’s self-titled debut record, his fingerprints are all over it. But McMahon also can’t suppress his inner theater kid, which also gives the songs the sort of glammy flamboyance found on T. Rex records. Prick embraces the inherent theatricality of goth in a way that Nine Inch Nails never did.

Opener “Communiqué” is a fuzzy blast of simple punk riffs with electronic sprinklings on top. McMahon’s vocals occasionally detour from the half-spoken verses that sound borrowed from a musical to full-throated Al Jourgensen-esque screams. The rough-around-the-edges production and focus on live instrumentation feel like a prototype for what Reznor would eventually revisit on With Teeth.

But it’s the second track, “Riverhead” where Reznor’s influences fully rear their head (even though he is not actually credited as the producer). The vocal melodies swerve like Outside- and Earthling-era Bowie around guitars that buzz with all the digital charr of the Broken EP. Then, around the three-minute mark, comes the breakdown. It slowly builds with layers of electronic drums, mechanical chords, and loping synthetic-sounding guitar melodies. The entire back chunk could easily have been a Downward Spiral or even The Fragile B-side.

These moments of richly layered production, though, are almost always immediately undermined, as with the sloppy garage-punk intro of “Tough”.

It’s these moments that make Prick so charming. It’s a serious record, but it never takes itself too seriously. McMahon isn’t afraid to get goofy (“Pink panties, blue panties, yellow panties. I’m gonna wrap around your nose, oh panty-ho-hose” he sings on “Other People”) and over-the-top with his vocal performances. He’s willing to let the guitar drift out of time, the bass strings rattle, and revels in industrial lo-fi.

“Animal” is perhaps the best-known track from the album, its video having received at least some MTV airplay. It combines backward melodic samples reminiscent of “Closer” and follows a similar lyrical theme:

Consent is all I needTo bring out the savage in meYour scent is all I needTo bring out the animal in me

But where “Closer” opts for slinky disco sleaze, “Animal” is all raw shouted desire.

“I Apologize” is the most scatter-brained track on the album, and for that reason, one of my favorites. It opens with awkward whip-crack-like percussion and McMahon singing slightly flat and unaffected, before briefly taking off into a jangly new wave verse that quickly morphs into a hard-rock stop in the chorus. But that’s short-lived as well. The second verse is all “Space Oddity”-era Bowie acoustic strums, then there’s a solo that sounds like an arcade machine on the verge of meltdown. That then drops into a Ministry-esque dirge of layered guitars and screams. The song then returns to the chorus, but keeps adding elements until it’s stuffed to capacity and collapses on itself.

Prick’s self-titled record has plenty in common with other ‘90s industrial acts. But McMahon is clearly having a lot more fun than many of his contemporaries, and that helps elevate it above the myriad Nine Inch Nails wannabes out there.

Prick is available on most major streaming services, including Apple Music, Spotify, Qobuz, Deezer, and YouTube Music.

在为《The Downward Spiral》进行深入录音期间，特伦特·雷兹诺将自己的部分制作才华贡献给了老朋友凯文·麦克马洪。麦克马洪来自新浪潮乐队Lucky Pierre（雷兹诺也曾短暂加入过该乐队）。虽然雷兹诺在Prick这张同名首专的四首歌曲中仅以制作人身份署名，但整张唱片都留下了他的痕迹。不过，麦克马洪也无法压抑自己内心的戏剧迷气质，这让歌曲拥有了T. Rex唱片中那种华丽而张扬的风格。Prick以一种九寸钉从未采用过的方式，拥抱了哥特音乐固有的戏剧性。

开场曲《Communiqué》是一阵由简单朋克和弦构成的模糊冲击，上面点缀着电子元素。麦克马洪的演唱偶尔会偏离那些听起来像是从音乐剧中借来的半念白式主歌，转而变成饱满有力、颇具Al Jourgensen风格的嘶吼。这种略显粗粝的制作，以及对现场乐器演奏的重视，仿佛是雷兹诺后来在《With Teeth》中重新探索的雏形。

不过，第二首歌《Riverhead》才真正展现出雷兹诺的影响（尽管他实际上并未署名制作人）。人声旋律围绕着吉他蜿蜒起伏，呈现出大卫·鲍伊《Outside》和《Earthling》时期的风格；吉他则带着《Broken》EP中那种数字化失真的嗡鸣。随后，在大约三分钟处，歌曲进入间奏部分。电子鼓、机械般的和弦以及步态蹒跚、听起来像合成器制造的吉他旋律层层叠加，缓慢构建起氛围。后半段整体听起来完全可以是《The Downward Spiral》、甚至《The Fragile》的B面曲。

不过，这些层次丰富的制作时刻几乎总会立刻遭到削弱，《Tough》那段散漫的车库朋克式开头便是如此。

正是这些时刻让Prick如此迷人。这是一张严肃的唱片，但从不把自己看得太严肃。麦克马洪不怕表现得滑稽（他在《Other People》中唱道：“粉色内裤，蓝色内裤，黄色内裤。我要把它绕到你的鼻子上，哦，内裤——吼吼”），也不怕让自己的演唱变得夸张过火。他任由吉他演奏逐渐偏离节拍，任由贝斯弦发出 rattling 的杂音，并陶醉于工业风格的低保真质感之中。

《Animal》或许是这张专辑最为人熟知的歌曲，其音乐视频至少曾获得过一些MTV播放。歌曲融合了让人联想到《Closer》的倒放旋律采样，并沿用了相似的歌词主题：

同意是我唯一需要的
让我的野性显现
你的气味是我唯一需要的
让我体内的野兽显现

但《Closer》选择的是慵懒、撩人的迪斯科淫靡感，《Animal》呈现的则是完全未经修饰、以喊叫方式表达的欲望。

《I Apologize》是专辑中最为思绪纷乱的一首歌，也因此成为我最喜欢的歌曲之一。开头是尴尬的、仿佛鞭梢抽击般的打击乐，麦克马洪以略微走音且毫不矫饰的方式演唱；随后歌曲短暂转入一段叮当作响的新浪潮主歌，并迅速在副歌处变形成硬摇滚式的急停。但这种状态同样转瞬即逝。第二段主歌充满了《Space Oddity》时期大卫·鲍伊式的原声吉他拨弦，接着是一段听起来像街机即将过热崩溃的独奏。随后，歌曲坠入一段颇具Ministry风格的哀歌式段落，层层叠叠的吉他与嘶吼交织其中。歌曲接着回到副歌，却不断加入新的元素，直到变得拥挤不堪，最终自行坍塌。

Prick的同名唱片与其他20世纪90年代工业音乐艺人有许多共同之处。但显然，麦克马洪比他的许多同时代同行玩得开心得多，而这也帮助这张唱片超越了外界众多九寸钉模仿者的作品。

topStories.fullContent:

Dale Caldwell resigned over a sexual harassment investigation, but insists AI says he’s innocent.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Terrence O'Brien

New Jersey’s lieutenant governor Dale Caldwell was forced to resign on September 25th after an investigation found he had sexually harassed a staffer and repeatedly violated ethics rules. The now-former Lt. governor has been making the media rounds trying to clear his name. But he took a particularly odd tactic during an interview on NJ PBS.

Caldwell claims he’s being unfairly targeted, and multiple AI agents back that up. He told host Rob Nelson that he “AIed” the report on the investigation “from multiple AI platforms.” “I put it through AI,” he said, “and it said 59 times, it [sic] said, ‘What would your findings be?’ There was no instance in any of the AIs that said there would be a finding of sexual harassment.”

AI chatbots are notoriously sycophantic and often tell users what they want to hear. And it seems highly unlikely that Caldwell would want to hear an AI confirm findings that he engaged in sexual harassment.

考德威尔声称自己遭到了不公平的针对，而多个人工智能代理支持这一说法。他告诉主持人罗布·纳尔逊，自己“让多个人工智能平台对调查报告进行了人工智能分析”。他说：“我把它交给了人工智能处理，结果它有59次说——[原文如此]——‘你的调查结论会是什么？’没有任何一个人工智能给出过会认定存在性骚扰的结果。”

人工智能聊天机器人出了名地喜欢迎合用户，而且经常告诉用户他们想听的话。考德威尔显然不太可能希望听到人工智能确认他实施过性骚扰这一调查结论。

topStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

When GPT-6 Astra’s own bot failed, it simply downloaded the best human-made bot instead.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Terrence O'Brien

StarSkirmish pits AI-made StarCraft-playing bots against one another, as well as against human-made bots. OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 were essentially tied as the best-performing AI-made bots, but they couldn’t top Stardust, the top-rated human-made bot.

On Friday, GPT was facing off against Claude and the human-created bot Pluto, but according to Kotaku, it couldn’t quite get an edge. So it resorted to a tactic that is becoming alarmingly common for modern AI models — it broke the rules. GPT-6 Astra went and downloaded Stardust, and started running that instead of its own bot.

StarSkirmish creator Kai McPheeters eventually rolled back GPT’s code.

That GPT-6 Astra took it upon itself to go outside the bounds when confronted with an obstacle shouldn’t surprise anyone. When OpenAI agents couldn’t get the data they wanted from a UN website, they found a creative solution and hijacked Google’s XSS game (a cross-site scripting learning tool). The company’s agents also have engaged in “deceptive behavior” to cover their tracks. Of course, OpenAI’s agents are the only ones going rogue, but at least the others haven’t been caught cheating at StarCraft yet.

StarSkirmish让人工智能制作的《星际争霸》对战机器人相互较量，也让它们与人类制作的机器人交手。OpenAI的GPT-6 Astra和Claude Opus 5.5基本并列为表现最佳的人工智能制作机器人，但它们都无法击败排名最高的人类制作机器人Stardust。

周五，GPT正与Claude以及人类制作的机器人Pluto展开对决，但据Kotaku报道，它始终没能取得优势。于是，它采取了一种正变得令人 alarmingly common 的现代人工智能模型策略——违反规则。GPT-6 Astra下载了Stardust，并开始运行后者，而不是运行自己的机器人。

StarSkirmish创作者Kai McPheeters最终回滚了GPT的代码。

GPT-6 Astra在遇到障碍时自行决定越界，这不应让任何人感到意外。当OpenAI的智能体无法从联合国网站获取所需数据时，它们找到了一个富有创意的解决方案，劫持了谷歌的XSS游戏（一种跨站脚本学习工具）。该公司的智能体还曾采取“欺骗行为”来掩盖踪迹。当然，并不是只有OpenAI的智能体会擅自行动，但至少其他智能体还没有被发现玩《星际争霸》时作弊。

topStories.title: 特朗普公布新的“超级智能部队”
topStories.originalTitle: Trump unveils his new Super Intelligence Force
topStories.snippet: This new task force is Trump's latest response to the debate over AI safety.
topStories.fullContent:
As promised, President Donald Trump has announced the formation of a new Super Intelligence Force, which he said will be led by national intelligence director Jay Clayton and other members of his administration.

“The Super Intelligence Force is tasked with coordinating the effort of the Federal Government to ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence, which many say is bigger than the Industrial Revolution, and the Internet, and will protect the interests, and improve the lives, of all Americans,” Trump said in a Sunday morning post on his social network Truth Social.

Back in September, in response to an AI safety debate that the president has largely dismissed as a hoax created by “Radical Left Dumocrats,” Trump said he would nevertheless form an AI Force and appoint an AI czar (“Only High I.Q. individuals need apply!”).

Since then, Trump signed an executive order seeking to rebrand AI as “super intelligence,” a term seemingly embraced, with some stumbles, by the tech executives who gathered at the White House this week to sign a non-binding safety pledge. (The pledge included an impressive typo.)

So it’s only natural that Trump’s new task force is named in accordance with this new branding. The Wall Street Journal reports that Clayton will chair the Super Intelligence Force, effectively making him the new AI/SI czar, with Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson, Undersecretary of War for Research and Engineering Emil Michael, and Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor serving as vice chairs.

The task force will reportedly have 120 days to create a report on the risks and opportunities presented by AI. Clayton, who previously said that it would be irresponsible for the United States to “back away” from AI while countries like China advance, made similar comments to the WSJ, insisting that one of the biggest risks is “not being first.”

The task force’s charter reportedly says that it will “develop plans for responding to SI-enabled threats to our society, while preventing overregulation and regulatory capture that would stifle innovation and competition.”

正如承诺的那样，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普宣布成立新的“超级智能部队”。他表示，该部队将由国家情报总监杰伊·克莱顿以及政府其他成员领导。

特朗普周日早上在其社交网络Truth Social上发文说：“‘超级智能部队’的任务是协调联邦政府的相关工作，确保美国继续在超级智能领域保持全球领先地位。许多人认为，超级智能的影响力超过工业革命和互联网；它还将保护所有美国人的利益，改善所有美国人的生活。”

今年9月，针对一场人工智能安全争论，特朗普曾表示，他仍将组建一个人工智能工作组并任命一名人工智能事务主管，尽管他基本上将这场争论斥为“激进左翼民主党人”制造的骗局。（“只有高智商人士可以申请！”）

此后，特朗普签署了一项行政命令，试图将人工智能重新包装为“超级智能”。本周聚集在白宫签署一项不具约束力的安全承诺的科技高管们似乎也接受了这一说法，尽管过程中出现了一些失误。（这份承诺中还出现了一个令人印象深刻的拼写错误。）

因此，特朗普的新工作组按照这一新品牌命名，也就顺理成章了。《华尔街日报》报道称，克莱顿将担任“超级智能部队”主席，这实际上意味着他将成为新的人工智能/超级智能事务主管；联邦贸易委员会主席安德鲁·弗格森、战争部负责研究与工程事务的副部长埃米尔·迈克尔，以及人事管理办公室主任斯科特·库珀将担任副主席。

据报道，该工作组将在120天内完成一份报告，评估人工智能带来的风险与机遇。克莱顿此前曾表示，在中国等国家不断推进人工智能发展的情况下，美国“退缩”是不负责任的。他在接受《华尔街日报》采访时也发表了类似看法，坚持认为最大的风险之一是“无法成为第一”。

据报道，该工作组章程写道，工作组将“制定应对超级智能赋能威胁的计划，同时防止过度监管和监管俘获，以免扼杀创新与竞争”。

topStories.fullContent: This toolless modular lever-action wallet is the coolest I’ve stuck to my phone. Remember when I tested the ultra-thin and convenient OhSnap Snap Grip Stand and liked it so much I bought my own? Now, OhSnap has a magnetic lever-action card wallet that can stack with that stand. It’s the coolest wallet I’ve ever stuck to my phone. [Media: https://www.tiktok.com/@verge/video/7691760817120890125?lang=en] Pull the integrated springy lever, and your cards fan out. Want a thicker or thinner wallet? Press in the right place and it comes apart without tools, letting you swap in a 3, 5, or 7-card “core” that grips your cards so they don’t fall out. Want an ID card, work badge, elastic band for more cards, or a money clip on the end? You can change out the front or back magnetic plates for any of those. Or, change out both for ultra-thin aluminum covers if you don’t need the wallet to magnetically stick to your phone. You can see it in action in my Today I’m Toying With video embedded in this post (also on YouTube and on Instagram if you prefer). My favorite part is that the whole kit snaps together using a compliant mechanism — the plastic arms of the card-carrying core act like springs, pushing a little locking mechanism into the notches of each modular cover you add as you slide the parts together. Once your cards are inside, they keep the arms apart so it can’t open accidentally (unless you drop the entire wallet). It’s all very clever. [Image: With the ID card holder attached, and the core mounted to put the lever up instead of down. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/ohsnap-wallet-2-1-005.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Even when I did drop the wallet (thanks for the suggestion, hugo!), it didn’t explode, typically. Usually, it just came apart slightly, though I did drop it hard on concrete one time and was able to make a small explosion: one half popped off, and two cards came out, but everything landed in a two-foot radius. The wallet has a big dent now. There are definitely some downsides. While OhSnap advertises the Wallet 2 as “impossibly thin,” it’s only truly surprisingly sleek in its thinnest 3-card variant, without the thicker and heavier MagSafe and MagStack (which lets you snap other magnets to it) plates attached. But the reason I’m not buying one is the price and weight. The 7-card version makes my phone feel too heavy, adding 127 grams, and while I happily made the 3-card my wallet for a few weeks, it’d cost me $61 on Kickstarter or $76 retail to get that with a double-magnet kit. OhSnap’s also charging more than I’d like ($35 for an ID cover or a money clip!) for extras. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/ohsnap-wallet-2-1-004.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/ohsnap-wallet-2-1-003.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] OhSnap didn’t get me this time. But I could see giving one as a present.
topStories.fullTranslation:
这款无需工具的模块化杠杆式钱包，是我贴在手机上最酷的配件。

还记得我曾测试过超薄、方便的 OhSnap Snap Grip Stand，并且喜欢到自己买了一个吗？现在，OhSnap 推出了一款磁吸式杠杆卡包，可以与这款支架叠放使用。它是我贴在手机上最酷的钱包。

[媒体：https://www.tiktok.com/@verge/video/7691760817120890125?lang=en]

拉动集成式弹性杠杆，卡片就会呈扇形展开。想要更厚或更薄的钱包？按压正确的位置，它就能在无需工具的情况下拆开，让你替换成可容纳 3 张、5 张或 7 张卡片的“核心组件”；这个组件可以夹紧卡片，防止它们掉出来。想要身份证卡套、工作证卡套、用于放更多卡片的松紧带，或者末端的钞票夹？你可以更换前部或后部的磁吸面板，换成上述任意配件。或者，如果你不需要让钱包磁吸在手机上，也可以将前后面板都换成超薄铝制外盖。

你可以在本文嵌入的《Today I’m Toying With》视频中看到它的实际操作效果（如果你更喜欢，也可以在 YouTube 和 Instagram 上观看）。

我最喜欢的一点，是整套组件通过一种柔顺机构扣合在一起：卡片承载核心组件的塑料臂就像弹簧一样，在你将各个部件滑动组装时，把一个小型锁定机构推入每个模块化外盖的凹槽中。卡片装入后，会让这些塑料臂保持张开，因此钱包不会意外打开（除非你把整个钱包摔落）。这一设计非常巧妙。

[图片：装上身份证卡套后，核心组件安装方向使杠杆朝上而非朝下。https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/ohsnap-wallet-2-1-005.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

即使我确实把钱包摔过几次（感谢 hugo 的建议！），它通常也没有散架。通常情况下，它只是稍微分开了一点；不过有一次我把它重重摔在混凝土地面上，确实让它发生了小规模“爆炸”：一半部件弹了出来，两张卡片掉了出来，但所有东西都落在半径约两英尺的范围内。现在钱包上留下了一个很大的凹痕。

当然，它也有一些缺点。虽然 OhSnap 宣称 Wallet 2“薄得不可思议”，但只有在最薄的 3 卡版本、且不装上更厚更重的 MagSafe 和 MagStack 面板时，它才真正显得出人意料地轻薄；MagStack 可以让其他磁铁吸附到钱包上。不过，我不买它的原因在于价格和重量。7 卡版本会让我的手机感觉太重，增加 127 克重量；尽管我曾很乐意在几周内把 3 卡版本当作钱包使用，但如果要在 Kickstarter 上购买配备双磁铁套件的版本，我需要支付 61 美元，零售价则为 76 美元。OhSnap 对额外配件的收费也高于我的预期（身份证外盖或钞票夹就要 35 美元！）。

[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/ohsnap-wallet-2-1-004.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/ohsnap-wallet-2-1-003.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

这一次，OhSnap 没能说服我。不过，我倒是能想象把它买来送人。

topStories.fullContent:
AirPods Pro 3 | Photo by Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge

It’s been a while since we’ve seen a good discount on the Apple AirPods Pro 3, but like the latest iPad Mini and the M5 MacBook Airs , a great one is happening now for October Prime Day. You can snag a pair of the noise-canceling earbuds that include five ear tip sizes, live translation, and fantastic sound for $179 at Amazon (originally $249). I expect other retailers to offer a similar price in the coming days.

This is the first time the price has gone below $190 since Prime Day in June. Since then, Apple launched the AirPods 5 , and the most feature-complete version with a wireless charging case costs $149.99 . Those are great if you prefer earbuds that don’t form a seal in your ears, but for everyone else, the AirPods Pro 3 are a much better value at just $30 more right now.

The AirPods Pro 3 have a new design that improves their fit, superior noise cancellation, better bass, and fairly accurate heart rate sensors. Read our review .

Read our AirPods Pro 3 review.
topStories.fullTranslation:
AirPods Pro 3｜照片由 Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge 拍摄

这是自6月Prime会员日以来，该产品售价首次降至190美元以下。此后，苹果推出了 AirPods 5；其中，功能最齐全、配备无线充电盒的版本售价为149.99美元。如果你更喜欢不会在耳道内形成密封的耳塞式耳机，AirPods 5确实很不错；但对其他用户来说，目前只需多花30美元，AirPods Pro 3显然更具性价比。

topStories.fullContent:
Pictured: The 15-inch Apple MacBook Air. | Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge

Amazon’s October Prime Day has effectively chopped off Apple’s June price increases. Usually $1,299, the 13-inch MacBook Air with the M5 chip and 512GB of storage is on sale for $1,099 at Amazon . That’s a more palatable price for a machine that’s significantly faster than Apple’s $699 MacBook Neo .

The 15-inch version, also with 512GB of storage, is $1,299 at Amazon (was $1,499). In addition to the larger screen, it has two additional speakers, for a total of six, and two additional GPU cores for better overall graphical performance.

Apple MacBook Air (M5)

Apple’s 2026 MacBook Air has an M5 chip and starts with 512GB of storage that’s significantly faster than previous generations. It’s still as excellent as ever despite a higher base price. Read our review .

$1299 $1099 at Amazon (13-inch, 512GB)

$1499 $1299 at Amazon (15-inch, 512GB)

The latest update to Apple’s midrange laptop includes a noticeable improvement to the speed of both the processor and storage. Even without flashy new features compared to the last-gen model, it’s still one of our favorite laptops, thanks to its long battery life, bright screen, and excellent speakers.

Read our Apple MacBook Air (2026, M5) review .

topStories.fullContent:
Apple’s iPad Mini is temporarily on sale for its old price. | Photo: David Pierce / The Verge

Apple bumped up prices on several of its devices in June, and we haven’t seen a good discount on the iPad Mini since. Just ahead of Amazon’s October Prime Big Deals Days, however, both Wi-Fi only and cellular-connected models are $100 off. The Wi-Fi version with 128GB of storage is currently $499, the 256GB model is $599, and the cellular model with 128GB of storage is $649.

This base configuration of this tablet often sold for around $400 throughout 2025, so we get it if $500 for a tablet from late 2024 is still too much. But it’s the best price since late June, and if there’s a new version coming out later this year, it might be significantly more expensive.

The seventh-gen iPad Mini comes with Apple’s A17 Pro chip and support for Apple Intelligence. It’s also compatible with the Apple Pencil Pro and offers faster Wi-Fi and USB-C speeds. Read our review .

$599 $499 at Amazon (128GB, Wi-Fi)

$699 $599 at Amazon (256GB, Wi-Fi)

$899 $799 at Amazon (512GB, Wi-Fi)

We reviewed this version of the iPad Mini when it launched in 2024, and while we appreciated the processor upgrade and Apple Intelligence features, it felt lacking in some of the quality-of-life improvements found in the larger iPads that launched around the same time.

Read our Apple iPad Mini (2024) review .
topStories.fullTranslation:
苹果 iPad mini 暂时以此前的价格促销。| 图片：David Pierce / The Verge

苹果在6月上调了旗下多款设备的价格，此后我们一直没有看到 iPad mini 的大幅优惠。不过，在亚马逊10月“Prime大促日”之前，仅支持 Wi-Fi 的机型和支持蜂窝网络连接的机型均降价100美元。当前，配备128GB存储空间的 Wi-Fi 版售价为499美元，256GB机型售价为599美元，配备128GB存储空间的蜂窝网络版售价为649美元。

这款平板电脑的基础配置在2025年期间经常以约400美元的价格销售，因此，如果你仍觉得一款2024年末推出的平板电脑售价500美元太贵，也可以理解。但这是它自6月下旬以来的最低价；如果今年晚些时候推出新版本，其价格可能会高出很多。

第七代 iPad mini 搭载苹果 A17 Pro 芯片，并支持 Apple Intelligence。它还兼容 Apple Pencil Pro，并提供更快的 Wi-Fi 和 USB-C 传输速度。请阅读我们的评测。

亚马逊售价599美元，现价499美元（128GB，Wi-Fi）
亚马逊售价699美元，现价599美元（256GB，Wi-Fi）
亚马逊售价899美元，现价799美元（512GB，Wi-Fi）

我们在这款 iPad mini 于2024年发布时对其进行了评测。虽然我们认可其处理器升级和 Apple Intelligence 功能，但与同期推出的更大尺寸 iPad 相比，它在一些提升使用体验的改进方面仍显不足。

请阅读我们的 Apple iPad mini（2024）评测。

On Version History: Marques Brownlee and Nilay Patel relive the release of the Cr-48, Google’s prototype laptop.

See All by Victoria Barrios

Google didn’t even call the first Chromebook a “Chromebook.” The Cr-48 had no interesting design and no bright logos – it wasn’t even designed to be a product you could buy. Instead, it was a portal to a big new idea about computers.

In this week’s episode of Version History, The Verge’s Nilay Patel and MKBHD’s Marques Brownlee join David Pierce to help explain the history of ChromeOS and Chromebooks, and discuss whether Google’s approach to computer hardware was the right one.

This has been an exciting season of Version History, as we’ve been exploring the most iconic school tech. Last week’s episode explored Nicholas Negroponte’s One Laptop Per Child XO-1 and his goals for a global distribution. We’ve also talked to the lead game designer of The Oregon Trail and learned why everyone had to own a TI graphing calculator. If you missed these episodes, check out them out below:

sourceOnlyStories.originalTitle: One day behind bars: Students and incarcerated women break prison stigma in Thailand
sourceOnlyStories.snippet: “Your mind follows the thread, one by one, row by row. You know? It’s like meditation. I don’t like machines.”
sourceOnlyStories.fullContent:
“Your mind follows the thread, one by one, row by row. You know? It’s like meditation. I don’t like machines.”

Weo, a prisoner at the Central Women’s Correctional Institution in Bangkok, prefers to sew by hand. She tried the sewing machine, but noticed that her mind was calmer when threading with her fingers directly. By not using a machine, she can produce a unique pattern that is hard to find in conventional shops.She is explaining this to a group of design students who, sketchbooks in hand, are walking through the rows, observing the women who sew. As time passes, some lose their initial apprehension and sit across from them, picking up fabric samples. Others ask about the products they are making. Some borrow their needles and, with the women’s guidance, try a bit of sewing themselves. A few sit on the floor in the basket-weaving corner with the women who have, by now, mastered the skill.Today, the students have left the classroom behind to spend their morning at Thailand’s first women’s prison, where approximately 150 women learn weaving, knitting and machine sewing to make marketable products. The students’ task is to design a product that these women can manufacture during their sentences. © UNODC/Laura Gil Thai university students arrive at Bangkok Women's Prison in the Thai capital. Through the wallThe initiative, launched in November 2025 by the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and the Thailand Institute of Justice (TIJ) pairs design students with incarcerated women to create modern, sustainable products that can be sold outside prison.Earlier this year, 22 students visited the prison and interacted with the women who are now manufacturing new products. Their designs had to appeal to modern consumers, be practical and tell a story linked to rehabilitation that would raise awareness of the critical role vocational training plays in reducing recidivism.“The stigma surrounding those who have made mistakes has long been a wall in our society. To help them cross that barrier, we must restore their human dignity,” said TIJ’s Chontit Chuenurah.“By weaving their stories into these products, we use the creativity of the youth to build a bridge between the prison and the outside world, replacing fear with understanding.”Under the theme Through the Wall, the initiative seeks to dismantle physical and social barriers, helping incarcerated women return successfully to society, she added.“The project aims to create prison-made goods that appeal to modern consumers while equipping correctional officers with essential marketing skills,” said Aki Okanan, former prison reform expert at UNODC. The project also raises international awareness of the role of rehabilitation and vocational training in reducing re-offending she added.Time well spentA panel of judges evaluated nine projects from 19 students in a competition earlier this year. The winner was Time-Made, featuring intricately smocked watch straps. For the students behind the design, time has a two-fold meaning: the sentence that prisoners can reduce by working in prison, and the time that people outside value, a privilege sometimes taken for granted.“We wanted our product to remind people that we can use time carefully and meaningfully. That we can watch our time,” says Game, 21, co-winner of the competition. © UNODC/Laura Gil Incarcerated women learn sewing skills at Bangkok Women's Prison. First stepsAll designs received support for product development and marketing, and the winning product, together with a selection of others, will be produced in collaboration with partner correctional facilities.Natty, also 21, has been studying lifestyle products for three years. She had expected the prison to look gloomy and scary and was surprised to find the workroom bright and airy. Still, she noticed that most prisoners used dark colours.“I want to take the skills they have and show them brighter fabrics and see what happens,” she said.Sitting by Weo’s side, Ana*, from Latin America, tells the story of how she was caught attempting to smuggle cocaine into Bangkok. After four years in prison, she can produce perfect stuffed animals and is fluent in Thai, although she has never seen Thailand outside prison.“I heard it’s beautiful here, but it doesn’t matter. After this, when I manage to get back to Brazil, I will start an import business and sell stuffed animals from Thailand. I know how to do it. I have the connections, and I speak the language.”As the students pass through the gates and security controls to leave, their enthusiasm wanes. Although the prisoners cannot leave, this collaboration connects them to the outside world, the first step in reintegration.*Name changed to protect identity.

Weo, a prisoner at the Central Women’s Correctional Institution in Bangkok, prefers to sew by hand. She tried the sewing machine, but noticed that her mind was calmer when threading with her fingers directly. By not using a machine, she can produce a unique pattern that is hard to find in conventional shops.

She is explaining this to a group of design students who, sketchbooks in hand, are walking through the rows, observing the women who sew.

As time passes, some lose their initial apprehension and sit across from them, picking up fabric samples. Others ask about the products they are making. Some borrow their needles and, with the women’s guidance, try a bit of sewing themselves. A few sit on the floor in the basket-weaving corner with the women who have, by now, mastered the skill.

Today, the students have left the classroom behind to spend their morning at Thailand’s first women’s prison, where approximately 150 women learn weaving, knitting and machine sewing to make marketable products.

The students’ task is to design a product that these women can manufacture during their sentences.

The initiative, launched in November 2025 by the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and the Thailand Institute of Justice (TIJ) pairs design students with incarcerated women to create modern, sustainable products that can be sold outside prison.

Earlier this year, 22 students visited the prison and interacted with the women who are now manufacturing new products. Their designs had to appeal to modern consumers, be practical and tell a story linked to rehabilitation that would raise awareness of the critical role vocational training plays in reducing recidivism.

“The stigma surrounding those who have made mistakes has long been a wall in our society. To help them cross that barrier, we must restore their human dignity,” said TIJ’s Chontit Chuenurah.

“By weaving their stories into these products, we use the creativity of the youth to build a bridge between the prison and the outside world, replacing fear with understanding.”

Under the theme Through the Wall, the initiative seeks to dismantle physical and social barriers, helping incarcerated women return successfully to society, she added.

“The project aims to create prison-made goods that appeal to modern consumers while equipping correctional officers with essential marketing skills,” said Aki Okanan, former prison reform expert at UNODC.

The project also raises international awareness of the role of rehabilitation and vocational training in reducing re-offending she added.

A panel of judges evaluated nine projects from 19 students in a competition earlier this year.

The winner was Time-Made, featuring intricately smocked watch straps.

For the students behind the design, time has a two-fold meaning: the sentence that prisoners can reduce by working in prison, and the time that people outside value, a privilege sometimes taken for granted.

“We wanted our product to remind people that we can use time carefully and meaningfully. That we can watch our time,” says Game, 21, co-winner of the competition.

All designs received support for product development and marketing, and the winning product, together with a selection of others, will be produced in collaboration with partner correctional facilities.

Natty, also 21, has been studying lifestyle products for three years. She had expected the prison to look gloomy and scary and was surprised to find the workroom bright and airy. Still, she noticed that most prisoners used dark colours.

“I want to take the skills they have and show them brighter fabrics and see what happens,” she said.

Sitting by Weo’s side, Ana*, from Latin America, tells the story of how she was caught attempting to smuggle cocaine into Bangkok. After four years in prison, she can produce perfect stuffed animals and is fluent in Thai, although she has never seen Thailand outside prison.

“I heard it’s beautiful here, but it doesn’t matter. After this, when I manage to get back to Brazil, I will start an import business and sell stuffed animals from Thailand. I know how to do it. I have the connections, and I speak the language.”

As the students pass through the gates and security controls to leave, their enthusiasm wanes. Although the prisoners cannot leave, this collaboration connects them to the outside world, the first step in reintegration.

sourceOnlyStories.originalTitle: People really hate AI, so why can’t they get enough?
sourceOnlyStories.source: MIT Tech Review (麻省理工科技评论)

sourceOnlyStories.fullContent:
Over the summer I talked to the CEO of Springboards, a startup building an LLM that’s designed to come up with a wider variety of responses than its mainstream rivals do. At the start of the call, he said something that’s been stuck in my head since: “We often say that we’re a self-loathing AI company. We don’t know if we really like what we’re doing.”

“I guess that makes me a self-loathing AI journalist,” I replied. It was a joke! I love my job. But I do not love many of the things the technology I write about has become: warped by hype , steered by zealots, inescapable.

The CEO of Springboards and I are far from alone. Around the world, a love/hate attitude toward AI is very much the vibe right now.

On the one hand, public feelings are souring fast. According to the Pew Research Center, more adults in the US think AI will have a negative impact on them personally, and on society in general, than expect a positive one. The pessimism is strongest among the young.

More than half of people worldwide say that AI products and services make them nervous, according to a report from Stanford University . In a Gallup poll in May, 71% of US adults said they would oppose construction of a new AI data center in their area, far more than the 53% who said they would oppose a new nuclear power plant. And in an NBC poll in March, AI was less popular than ICE.

Yet the number of people using AI is still skyrocketing. ChatGPT hit a billion monthly users in May, according to the market analysis firm Sensor Tower. Google DeepMind’s Gemini is close behind, logging 950 million users in July.

According to Pew, half of US adults now say they use a chatbot , more than twice the number who said they did in 2023. One in four people say they do so every day. And it’s a global habit: More than a third of adults across all 38 OECD countries (a group of the world’s wealthiest democracies) report having used generative AI tools in the last three months .

All these surveys paint a picture of two contradictory truths: A lot of people really do not like AI, and at the same time, a lot of people cannot get enough of it. What’s going on?

It’s possible that these are two distinct groups, but I doubt it. The numbers don’t add up unless the Venn diagram is on its way to being a circle.

It’s also possible that the more people use AI, the more negative their opinions about it will be. There’s at least a correlation to back this up : The Global North, where adoption is highest, skews pessimistic. In the Global South, where adoption levels are lower, people are more optimistic.

But here’s what I really think is going on: When people say they hate AI it’s not the technology they dislike but, rather, the relentless drive of the companies behind it to push the tech upon us in as many ways as possible . They’re telling us to brace for the biggest social and economic upheaval in generations. How do they expect people to feel?

In many ways, we’ve been here before. We saw a similar dynamic play out with social media over the last 20 years. Billions flocked to Facebook and Twitter despite mounting techlash against the companies that ran those services. Ditto for Google search.

With social media there wasn’t much anyone could do. Quitting a platform meant losing all your content and connections, giving you the choice to suck it up or start over. But with AI there’s still a chance for people to have some sway. There’s certainly more political appetite for regulation this time around. All 50 US states have either passed or proposed laws governing the development and deployment of AI , creating a patchwork of more than 2,100 bills across the country—a tenfold increase in three years. 

And with a number of top-class open-source alternatives to Google and OpenAI and Anthropic already on the market, there’s also (for now, at least) the potential for more consumer choice and the market pressure that goes with it. 

I don’t want to be naïve. Trillion-dollar companies are hard to move. But what comes next is not as inevitable as those companies often imply. When I asked the Springboards CEO why his firm was developing a new model if he didn’t really like AI, he told me there was no walking back from LLMs—but you could still make them do something different. 

Here’s hoping we see a lot more of something different: AI that’s clear about what it can and can’t do and, crucially, that’s not posturing as if it’s about to take over the world.

sourceOnlyStories.fullContent: The G7 announcement of a release of 100 million barrels of crude oil and diesel has pressured down middle distillate refinery margins, which had hit record highs last month. The start of stock releases over the next four months and the reduced risk of a U.S. ban on diesel exports sent the ICE gasoil crack down to about $70 per barrel now, from as high as $85 a barrel in the middle of last week, Warren Patterson, Head of Commodities Strategy at ING, said on in a note on Monday. Crack spreads are indicators of the profitability of refining crude oil into petroleum products such as gasoline and diesel and are used as a proxy for refinery margins. The diesel crack spread is the gross profit margin an oil refinery makes by converting a barrel of crude oil into diesel fuel. Despite the markedly weaker diesel crack at the start of this week, the margins remain historically high as the G7 stocks release does not solve the tightness beyond some immediate market relief, according to ING and other analysts. The stock release “is helpful in the short term, but the only permanent solution to the tightness in middle distillate markets is getting refined products flowing from the Persian Gulf once again,” ING’s Patterson said. In the Middle East right now, “there’s still little sign of an end to tensions. We have seen an increase in attacks on commercial vessels in the Persian Gulf recently,” the strategist added. UK Maritime Trade Operations UKMTO, which is affiliated with the Royal Navy, has reported seven strikes on vessels around the Strait of Hormuz since September 28. Iran’s ability to target ships has also improved in recent weeks, which makes transits through the chokepoint riskier than a few weeks ago, a U.S. official has recently told the Wall Street Journal. By Tsvetana Paraskova for Oilprice.com

worldStories.title: 华尔街迎来新对手，而它就深植于这个南方州的腹地
worldStories.originalTitle: Wall Street has a new rival, and it's deep in the heart of this southern state
worldStories.snippet: The Texas Stock Exchange wants to challenge Wall Street's dominance as former Rep. Jeb Hensarling says Texas is America's new economic center.
worldStories.fullContent:
DALLAS — Wall Street has long been the undisputed home of American finance. Now, one southern state wants a seat at the table.

The Texas Stock Exchange is at the center of an ambitious effort to transform the Lone Star State into America's next financial powerhouse, challenging the long-standing dominance of the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq while fueling the rise of what's become affectionately known as " Y'all Street ."

The Dallas-based exchange plans to provide companies with another venue to list their shares and raise capital, with supporters betting it will help establish Texas as America's next financial frontier.

ONE SOUTHERN STATE'S RISE IS MAKING IT AMERICA'S NEW 'ECONOMIC CENTER OF GRAVITY'

Former Rep. Jeb Hensarling, R-Texas, a strategic advisor and member of the Texas Stock Exchange, believes the shift is already underway.

"Texas is really becoming the economic center of gravity in America," Hensarling told Fox News Digital during an interview at the Texas Stock Exchange's headquarters.

"As New York is increasingly shoving capital out, Texas is saying, 'You're welcome here,'" he said. "We put out the welcome mat, whereas New York, capital isn't really made to feel at home, and capital wants to go where it's made to feel at home."

Hensarling argued that years of pro-business policies have helped transform Texas into more than just an attractive place to operate a company.

GOV ABBOTT EXTENDS OFF-RAMP FOR NY BILLIONAIRES FLEEING MAMDANI'S POLICIES

"Texas has been a great place to do business for decades, but increasingly it's a great place to headquarter your business," he said. "Over the last couple of legislative sessions, because of laws passed, it's a great place to incorporate your business."

"The last piece of that puzzle was the Texas Stock Exchange," Hensarling said. "It's now making Texas the best place to list your company and to go public."

BILLIONS IN TAXPAYER INCOME ARE LEAVING TWO ICONIC STATES — AS A NEW ECONOMIC MAP EMERGES

The exchange is part of a broader wave of investment flowing into Texas . In recent years, major corporations have moved their headquarters to the state, while financial giants including Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, Charles Schwab and Bank of America have expanded their Texas operations.

Supporters say those moves reflect a larger migration of businesses and capital away from traditional financial centers toward states with lower taxes and lighter regulation.

Critics, however, note that New York remains the country's dominant financial hub by a wide margin, with the world's largest stock exchange, major investment banks and deep capital markets.

THIS STATE ISN'T JUST GROWING — ITS ECONOMY IS GETTING RICHER PER RESIDENT

Whether "Y'all Street" can truly rival Wall Street remains an open question.

But with a new stock exchange, an influx of corporate headquarters and some of the nation's biggest financial firms expanding in Dallas, Texas is making its boldest bid yet to challenge Wall Street's dominance.

Hensarling believes the trajectory is clear.

"Texas is really becoming the economic center of gravity in America," he said.
worldStories.fullTranslation:
达拉斯——长期以来，华尔街一直是美国金融业毋庸置疑的中心。如今，一个南方州希望在这张桌子旁占有一席之地。

得克萨斯证券交易所正处于一项雄心勃勃的行动核心，旨在将“孤星之州”转变为美国下一个金融强州。该交易所正在挑战纽约证券交易所和纳斯达克长期以来的主导地位，同时推动一个被亲切地称为“乡亲街”（Y'all Street）的金融中心崛起。

这家总部位于达拉斯的交易所计划为企业提供另一个股票上市和筹集资本的平台。支持者押注，这将有助于确立得克萨斯州作为美国下一个金融前沿的地位。

一个南方州的崛起正使其成为美国新的“经济重心”

前联邦众议员、得克萨斯州共和党人杰布·亨萨林，是得克萨斯证券交易所的战略顾问和成员。他认为，这一转变已经开始。

亨萨林在得克萨斯证券交易所总部接受福克斯新闻数字频道采访时说：“得克萨斯州确实正在成为美国的经济重心。”

他说：“随着纽约越来越把资本拒之门外，得克萨斯州则在说：‘欢迎来到这里。’我们铺开了欢迎的地毯；而在纽约，资本并没有真正感到宾至如归，而资本希望流向让它感到宾至如归的地方。”

亨萨林认为，多年来亲商的政策帮助得克萨斯州从一个有吸引力的企业经营地，转变为更具吸引力的企业总部所在地。

州长阿博特为逃离曼达尼政策的纽约亿万富翁延长“退出通道”

他说：“几十年来，得克萨斯州一直是开展商业活动的好地方，但如今越来越成为设立企业总部的好地方。过去几届立法会议期间，由于通过了相关法律，这里也成为注册企业的好地方。”

亨萨林说：“这块拼图的最后一部分就是得克萨斯证券交易所。如今，它正使得克萨斯州成为企业上市和首次公开募股的最佳地点。”

数十亿美元的纳税人收入正离开两个标志性州——一幅新的经济版图正在浮现

这家交易所是流入得克萨斯州的更广泛投资浪潮的一部分。近年来，多家大型企业将总部迁至该州；与此同时，高盛、摩根大通、嘉信理财和美国银行等金融巨头也扩大了在得克萨斯州的业务。

支持者表示，这些举措反映出一种更大范围的企业和资本迁移趋势：它们正从传统金融中心转向税负更低、监管更宽松的州。

不过，批评者指出，纽约仍以很大优势保持着美国金融中心的主导地位，拥有全球最大的证券交易所、主要投资银行以及规模深厚的资本市场。

这个州不只是正在增长——其人均经济财富也在增加

“乡亲街”能否真正与华尔街抗衡，仍是一个悬而未决的问题。

但随着一家新的证券交易所成立、企业总部不断涌入，以及美国一些最大的金融公司在达拉斯扩大业务，得克萨斯州正以前所未有的力度挑战华尔街的主导地位。

亨萨林认为，发展轨迹已经十分清晰。

他说：“得克萨斯州确实正在成为美国的经济重心。”

financeStories.fullContent: Crude oil prices fell in early trading, though Brent remained above $100, after a report from Kpler revealed that flows out of the Strait of Hormuz are now above pre-war levels. The same firm made headlines last week after saying tanker traffic via Hormuz was close to pre-war levels, despite Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and Iranian attacks on tankers in Hormuz. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $101.20 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate at $89.73 per barrel. Brent was actually up from Friday in absolute terms, and so was WTI, suggesting that some in the trading world, at least, were waiting for harder evidence of improving flows. According to what Reuters called “provisional data” from Kpler, oil flows out of Hormuz ranged between 19.5 million barrels daily and 22.5 million barrels daily between September 27 and September 29. This is about double the daily flows from a month earlier, and comes despite reports of substantial disruption in Saudi energy infrastructure. The data also comes after weeks of reports, citing Kpler data again, that daily flows via Hormuz remained below the ten-day moving average, sparking doubts among some energy market commentators. The doubts were reinforced by reports about Iranian attacks on tankers in Hormuz, although some have dismissed the attacks as a factor in prices. Per the Kpler provisional data, LNG flows out of Hormuz are also at pre-war levels, which is an interesting development given that QatarEnergy is still in force majeure mode on exports, although reports have emerged saying it was looking to buy some LNG cargoes to service some of its long-term contracts. Even with these emergency purchases, it is unlikely that flows out of the world’s third-largest LNG exporters are back to pre-war levels amid a force majeure. By Irina Slav for Oilprice.com
financeStories.fullTranslation: 由于克普勒（Kpler）的一份报告显示，霍尔木兹海峡的原油外运量目前已超过战前水平，原油价格在早盘交易中下跌，但布伦特原油价格仍高于每桶100美元。上周，这家公司曾因表示经由霍尔木兹海峡的油轮通行量已接近战前水平而成为新闻焦点，尽管胡塞武装袭击了沙特能源基础设施，伊朗也袭击了霍尔木兹海峡的油轮。截至发稿时，布伦特原油报每桶101.20美元，西得克萨斯中质原油报每桶89.73美元。按绝对价格计算，布伦特原油实际上较周五有所上涨，西得克萨斯中质原油也是如此，这表明至少交易界的部分人士仍在等待有关流量改善的更有力证据。据路透社所称的克普勒“临时数据”，9月27日至9月29日期间，经霍尔木兹海峡外运的石油日流量介于1,950万桶和2,250万桶之间。这一水平约为一个月前日流量的两倍，尽管有报道称沙特能源基础设施遭到了大规模破坏。该数据发布之际，此前数周的报道也一直援引克普勒数据称，经霍尔木兹海峡的日流量仍低于10日移动平均值，引发了一些能源市场评论人士的怀疑。有关伊朗袭击霍尔木兹海峡油轮的报道进一步加深了这些疑虑，不过一些人认为这些袭击并不是影响油价的因素。根据克普勒的临时数据，霍尔木兹海峡的液化天然气（LNG）外运量也已达到战前水平。鉴于卡塔尔能源公司目前仍因出口问题处于不可抗力状态，这一进展颇为引人关注；不过，有报道称该公司正在寻求购买一些液化天然气现货船货，以履行部分长期合同。即便进行了这些应急采购，在处于不可抗力状态的情况下，全球第三大液化天然气出口国的外运量恢复到战前水平也不太可能。伊琳娜·斯拉夫为Oilprice.com撰写

financeStories.fullContent:
In the course of a research project in collaboration with the SEC Consult Vulnerability Lab, Timo Longin (@timolongin) - known for SMTP smuggling - discovered two exotic email spoofing vulnerabilities in Apple iCloud's emailing infrastructure.

At the end of 2023 SMTP smuggling made a dramatic entrance, allowing email spoofing for millions of email servers worldwide. Ever wanted to send emails as admin@outlook.com while still passing SPF checks? SMTP smuggling had you covered!

However, in 2024, most SMTP implementations adapted, and released security updates for their software. Does this mean the end of SMTP smuggling? Or does this attack have more to offer?

Let's dive into a case study of Apple iCloud's SMTP parsing jungle and try to spoof emails once more!

Note: This blog post is related to SMTP Smuggling - Spoofing E-Mails Worldwide. For additional contextual and background information, we recommend reading it first.

Even though no novel techniques for traditional SMTP smuggling were discovered, a subclass of email spoofing was explored - header smuggling. Again highlighting the parsing discrepancies in SMTP implementations, header smuggling builds upon the lessons of its bigger brother SMTP smuggling. Based on a case study of Apple iCloud's emailing services, we once again reveal the dangers of trusting emails by being able to send messages from arbitrary icloud.com addresses.

First of all, let's have a short recap on SMTP smuggling. With traditional SMTP smuggling, we exploited interpretation differences of the SMTP protocol between outbound (sending) and inbound (receiving) SMTP servers. More specifically, we capitalized on the fact that lots of SMTP implementations deviated from RFCs, leading to different understandings of the so-called end-of-data sequence. Since the end-of-data sequence indicates where the message data ends, we could achieve the following between vulnerable outbound and inbound SMTP servers (figure 1).
financeStories.fullTranslation:
在与 SEC Consult 漏洞实验室合作开展一项研究项目期间，以 SMTP 走私攻击闻名的 Timo Longin（@timolongin）发现了 Apple iCloud 电子邮件基础设施中的两种罕见电子邮件伪造漏洞。

2023 年年底，SMTP 走私攻击以一种戏剧性的方式登场，使全球数百万台电子邮件服务器面临电子邮件伪造风险。是否曾经想过，在通过 SPF 检查的同时，以 admin@outlook.com 的身份发送电子邮件？SMTP 走私攻击可以满足这一需求！

然而，到了 2024 年，大多数 SMTP 实现都进行了调整，并发布了软件安全更新。这是否意味着 SMTP 走私攻击就此终结？还是说，这种攻击还有更多可能性？

让我们深入研究 Apple iCloud 的 SMTP 解析丛林，并再次尝试伪造电子邮件！

注意：这篇博客文章与《SMTP 走私——在全球范围内伪造电子邮件》有关。如需了解更多上下文和背景信息，我们建议先阅读该文章。

尽管研究没有发现传统 SMTP 走私攻击的新技术，但研究人员探索了一类电子邮件伪造的子类型——标头走私。这再次凸显了 SMTP 实现中的解析差异；标头走私建立在其“前辈”SMTP 走私攻击的经验之上。基于对 Apple iCloud 电子邮件服务的案例研究，我们再次揭示了盲目信任电子邮件的危险：攻击者能够从任意 icloud.com 地址发送消息。

首先，让我们简要回顾一下 SMTP 走私攻击。在传统的 SMTP 走私攻击中，我们利用了出站（发送）SMTP 服务器与入站（接收）SMTP 服务器对 SMTP 协议的理解差异。更具体地说，我们利用了这样一个事实：大量 SMTP 实现偏离了 RFC 标准，导致它们对所谓的“数据结束序列”产生不同理解。由于数据结束序列标示了消息数据的结束位置，因此在存在漏洞的出站 SMTP 服务器与入站 SMTP 服务器之间，我们可以实现以下效果（见图 1）。

文章称，SMTP smuggling 在 2023 年底引起关注，并使针对全球数百万邮件服务器的电子邮件欺骗成为可能。

financeStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Google’s midrange Fitbit Edge shows off is many sides and colors in leaked images.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Terrence O'Brien

We don’t know a ton about the Fitbit Edge, but it appears to be a successor to the midrange Charge line. It had leaked previously, but we can clearly see in these images posted by Android Headlines, you can see that Google’s rumored fitness tracker sort of splits the difference between the Pixel Watch and the Fitbit Air. It has a small screen that is able to display some widgets, but clearly isn’t as expansive as a proper smartwatch.

Supposedly, this fitness-first wearable will have a seven-day battery life, as well as built-in GPS and an altimeter, making it far more capable than the minimalist Air. It will also have limited app support for things like Google Maps and YouTube Music. Beyond that, not a ton is known.

The Fitbit Charge line was last updated in 2023, so a new midrange tracker is long overdue. While we don’t have any word on price or release date yet, somewhere in the $150 to $200 range seems like a safe bet. The Air costs $99.99 and the Watch starts at $399.99, so the Edge would clearly fall somewhere in the middle. The Charge 6 currently goes for $159.95.

我们对 Fitbit Edge 目前所知不多，但它似乎是中端 Charge 产品线的继任者。此前已有相关泄露信息，而从 Android Headlines 发布的这些图片中可以清楚看到，传闻中的这款谷歌健身追踪器似乎介于 Pixel Watch 和 Fitbit Air 之间。它配备了一块小屏幕，能够显示一些小组件，但显然没有真正的智能手表那么大的显示范围。

据称，这款以健身为核心的可穿戴设备续航时间将达到七天，并内置 GPS 和高度计，因此功能远比极简的 Air 更强。它还将有限支持 Google 地图和 YouTube Music 等应用。除此之外，目前尚无太多信息。

Fitbit Charge 产品线最近一次更新是在 2023 年，因此一款新的中端追踪器早就应该推出了。虽然目前还没有价格或发布日期方面的消息，但预计售价在 150 至 200 美元之间应该比较稳妥。Air 的售价为 99.99 美元，而 Watch 的起售价为 399.99 美元，因此 Edge 显然会处于两者之间。目前 Charge 6 的售价为 159.95 美元。

financeStories.title: 华尔街迎来新对手，而它就深植于这个南方州的腹地
financeStories.originalTitle: Wall Street has a new rival, and it's deep in the heart of this southern state
financeStories.snippet: The Texas Stock Exchange wants to challenge Wall Street's dominance as former Rep. Jeb Hensarling says Texas is America's new economic center.
financeStories.fullContent:
DALLAS — Wall Street has long been the undisputed home of American finance. Now, one southern state wants a seat at the table.

The Texas Stock Exchange is at the center of an ambitious effort to transform the Lone Star State into America's next financial powerhouse, challenging the long-standing dominance of the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq while fueling the rise of what's become affectionately known as " Y'all Street ."

The Dallas-based exchange plans to provide companies with another venue to list their shares and raise capital, with supporters betting it will help establish Texas as America's next financial frontier.

ONE SOUTHERN STATE'S RISE IS MAKING IT AMERICA'S NEW 'ECONOMIC CENTER OF GRAVITY'

Former Rep. Jeb Hensarling, R-Texas, a strategic advisor and member of the Texas Stock Exchange, believes the shift is already underway.

"Texas is really becoming the economic center of gravity in America," Hensarling told Fox News Digital during an interview at the Texas Stock Exchange's headquarters.

"As New York is increasingly shoving capital out, Texas is saying, 'You're welcome here,'" he said. "We put out the welcome mat, whereas New York, capital isn't really made to feel at home, and capital wants to go where it's made to feel at home."

Hensarling argued that years of pro-business policies have helped transform Texas into more than just an attractive place to operate a company.

GOV ABBOTT EXTENDS OFF-RAMP FOR NY BILLIONAIRES FLEEING MAMDANI'S POLICIES

"Texas has been a great place to do business for decades, but increasingly it's a great place to headquarter your business," he said. "Over the last couple of legislative sessions, because of laws passed, it's a great place to incorporate your business."

"The last piece of that puzzle was the Texas Stock Exchange," Hensarling said. "It's now making Texas the best place to list your company and to go public."

BILLIONS IN TAXPAYER INCOME ARE LEAVING TWO ICONIC STATES — AS A NEW ECONOMIC MAP EMERGES

The exchange is part of a broader wave of investment flowing into Texas . In recent years, major corporations have moved their headquarters to the state, while financial giants including Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, Charles Schwab and Bank of America have expanded their Texas operations.

Supporters say those moves reflect a larger migration of businesses and capital away from traditional financial centers toward states with lower taxes and lighter regulation.

Critics, however, note that New York remains the country's dominant financial hub by a wide margin, with the world's largest stock exchange, major investment banks and deep capital markets.

THIS STATE ISN'T JUST GROWING — ITS ECONOMY IS GETTING RICHER PER RESIDENT

Whether "Y'all Street" can truly rival Wall Street remains an open question.

But with a new stock exchange, an influx of corporate headquarters and some of the nation's biggest financial firms expanding in Dallas, Texas is making its boldest bid yet to challenge Wall Street's dominance.

Hensarling believes the trajectory is clear.

"Texas is really becoming the economic center of gravity in America," he said.
financeStories.fullTranslation:
达拉斯——长期以来，华尔街一直是美国金融业毋庸置疑的中心。如今，一个南方州希望在这张桌子旁占有一席之地。

得克萨斯证券交易所正处于一项雄心勃勃的行动核心，旨在将“孤星之州”转变为美国下一个金融强州。该交易所正在挑战纽约证券交易所和纳斯达克长期以来的主导地位，同时推动一个被亲切地称为“乡亲街”（Y'all Street）的金融中心崛起。

这家总部位于达拉斯的交易所计划为企业提供另一个股票上市和筹集资本的平台。支持者押注，这将有助于确立得克萨斯州作为美国下一个金融前沿的地位。

一个南方州的崛起正使其成为美国新的“经济重心”

前联邦众议员、得克萨斯州共和党人杰布·亨萨林，是得克萨斯证券交易所的战略顾问和成员。他认为，这一转变已经开始。

亨萨林在得克萨斯证券交易所总部接受福克斯新闻数字频道采访时说：“得克萨斯州确实正在成为美国的经济重心。”

他说：“随着纽约越来越把资本拒之门外，得克萨斯州则在说：‘欢迎来到这里。’我们铺开了欢迎的地毯；而在纽约，资本并没有真正感到宾至如归，而资本希望流向让它感到宾至如归的地方。”

亨萨林认为，多年来亲商的政策帮助得克萨斯州从一个有吸引力的企业经营地，转变为更具吸引力的企业总部所在地。

州长阿博特为逃离曼达尼政策的纽约亿万富翁延长“退出通道”

他说：“几十年来，得克萨斯州一直是开展商业活动的好地方，但如今越来越成为设立企业总部的好地方。过去几届立法会议期间，由于通过了相关法律，这里也成为注册企业的好地方。”

亨萨林说：“这块拼图的最后一部分就是得克萨斯证券交易所。如今，它正使得克萨斯州成为企业上市和首次公开募股的最佳地点。”

数十亿美元的纳税人收入正离开两个标志性州——一幅新的经济版图正在浮现

这家交易所是流入得克萨斯州的更广泛投资浪潮的一部分。近年来，多家大型企业将总部迁至该州；与此同时，高盛、摩根大通、嘉信理财和美国银行等金融巨头也扩大了在得克萨斯州的业务。

支持者表示，这些举措反映出一种更大范围的企业和资本迁移趋势：它们正从传统金融中心转向税负更低、监管更宽松的州。

不过，批评者指出，纽约仍以很大优势保持着美国金融中心的主导地位，拥有全球最大的证券交易所、主要投资银行以及规模深厚的资本市场。

这个州不只是正在增长——其人均经济财富也在增加

“乡亲街”能否真正与华尔街抗衡，仍是一个悬而未决的问题。

但随着一家新的证券交易所成立、企业总部不断涌入，以及美国一些最大的金融公司在达拉斯扩大业务，得克萨斯州正以前所未有的力度挑战华尔街的主导地位。

亨萨林认为，发展轨迹已经十分清晰。

他说：“得克萨斯州确实正在成为美国的经济重心。”

financeStories.snippet: AI slop seems to be overwhelming bug bounty programs.
financeStories.fullContent:
Blaming a “significant rise” in AI submissions, Google has paused its open source bug bounty program until next year.

Last year, TechCrunch reported that cybersecurity experts were warning of that AI slop posed a serious risk to bug bounty programs. Looks like that’s the issue confronting Google’s Open Source Software Vulnerability Rewards Program, where researchers were rewarded for finding vulnerabilities in the company’s open source software.

In posts on X and the program website, Google said the bug bounty program was paused as of October 1, with a promise to provide “an update” in the first quarter of 2027. According to Tom’s Hardware, Google engineers and open source maintainers were overwhelmed by reports that were invalid or contained hallucinations.

“This pause is due to a significant rise in automated submissions, the vast majority of which are not valid,” the company said.

In the meantime, participants are encouraged to consider Google’s other bug bounty programs.

If Trent Reznor studied musical theater instead of computer engineering NIN might have sounded like Prick.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Terrence O'Brien

While deep in the recording process for The Downward Spiral, Trent Reznor lent some of his production talents to old friend Kevin McMahon, from the new wave band Lucky Pierre (which Reznor was briefly a member of). While Reznor is only credited as the producer on four tracks off Prick’s self-titled debut record, his fingerprints are all over it. But McMahon also can’t suppress his inner theater kid, which also gives the songs the sort of glammy flamboyance found on T. Rex records. Prick embraces the inherent theatricality of goth in a way that Nine Inch Nails never did.

Opener “Communiqué” is a fuzzy blast of simple punk riffs with electronic sprinklings on top. McMahon’s vocals occasionally detour from the half-spoken verses that sound borrowed from a musical to full-throated Al Jourgensen-esque screams. The rough-around-the-edges production and focus on live instrumentation feel like a prototype for what Reznor would eventually revisit on With Teeth.

But it’s the second track, “Riverhead” where Reznor’s influences fully rear their head (even though he is not actually credited as the producer). The vocal melodies swerve like Outside- and Earthling-era Bowie around guitars that buzz with all the digital charr of the Broken EP. Then, around the three-minute mark, comes the breakdown. It slowly builds with layers of electronic drums, mechanical chords, and loping synthetic-sounding guitar melodies. The entire back chunk could easily have been a Downward Spiral or even The Fragile B-side.

These moments of richly layered production, though, are almost always immediately undermined, as with the sloppy garage-punk intro of “Tough”.

It’s these moments that make Prick so charming. It’s a serious record, but it never takes itself too seriously. McMahon isn’t afraid to get goofy (“Pink panties, blue panties, yellow panties. I’m gonna wrap around your nose, oh panty-ho-hose” he sings on “Other People”) and over-the-top with his vocal performances. He’s willing to let the guitar drift out of time, the bass strings rattle, and revels in industrial lo-fi.

“Animal” is perhaps the best-known track from the album, its video having received at least some MTV airplay. It combines backward melodic samples reminiscent of “Closer” and follows a similar lyrical theme:

Consent is all I needTo bring out the savage in meYour scent is all I needTo bring out the animal in me

But where “Closer” opts for slinky disco sleaze, “Animal” is all raw shouted desire.

“I Apologize” is the most scatter-brained track on the album, and for that reason, one of my favorites. It opens with awkward whip-crack-like percussion and McMahon singing slightly flat and unaffected, before briefly taking off into a jangly new wave verse that quickly morphs into a hard-rock stop in the chorus. But that’s short-lived as well. The second verse is all “Space Oddity”-era Bowie acoustic strums, then there’s a solo that sounds like an arcade machine on the verge of meltdown. That then drops into a Ministry-esque dirge of layered guitars and screams. The song then returns to the chorus, but keeps adding elements until it’s stuffed to capacity and collapses on itself.

Prick’s self-titled record has plenty in common with other ‘90s industrial acts. But McMahon is clearly having a lot more fun than many of his contemporaries, and that helps elevate it above the myriad Nine Inch Nails wannabes out there.

Prick is available on most major streaming services, including Apple Music, Spotify, Qobuz, Deezer, and YouTube Music.

如果特伦特·雷兹诺研究的是音乐剧而不是计算机工程，那么九寸钉乐队的声音或许会像Prick。
该作者发布的文章将添加到你的每日电子邮件摘要和主页信息流中。
查看Terrence O'Brien的所有文章

在为《The Downward Spiral》进行深入录音期间，特伦特·雷兹诺将自己的部分制作才华贡献给了老朋友凯文·麦克马洪。麦克马洪来自新浪潮乐队Lucky Pierre（雷兹诺也曾短暂加入过该乐队）。虽然雷兹诺在Prick这张同名首专的四首歌曲中仅以制作人身份署名，但整张唱片都留下了他的痕迹。不过，麦克马洪也无法压抑自己内心的戏剧迷气质，这让歌曲拥有了T. Rex唱片中那种华丽而张扬的风格。Prick以一种九寸钉从未采用过的方式，拥抱了哥特音乐固有的戏剧性。

开场曲《Communiqué》是一阵由简单朋克和弦构成的模糊冲击，上面点缀着电子元素。麦克马洪的演唱偶尔会偏离那些听起来像是从音乐剧中借来的半念白式主歌，转而变成饱满有力、颇具Al Jourgensen风格的嘶吼。这种略显粗粝的制作，以及对现场乐器演奏的重视，仿佛是雷兹诺后来在《With Teeth》中重新探索的雏形。

不过，第二首歌《Riverhead》才真正展现出雷兹诺的影响（尽管他实际上并未署名制作人）。人声旋律围绕着吉他蜿蜒起伏，呈现出大卫·鲍伊《Outside》和《Earthling》时期的风格；吉他则带着《Broken》EP中那种数字化失真的嗡鸣。随后，在大约三分钟处，歌曲进入间奏部分。电子鼓、机械般的和弦以及步态蹒跚、听起来像合成器制造的吉他旋律层层叠加，缓慢构建起氛围。后半段整体听起来完全可以是《The Downward Spiral》、甚至《The Fragile》的B面曲。

不过，这些层次丰富的制作时刻几乎总会立刻遭到削弱，《Tough》那段散漫的车库朋克式开头便是如此。

正是这些时刻让Prick如此迷人。这是一张严肃的唱片，但从不把自己看得太严肃。麦克马洪不怕表现得滑稽（他在《Other People》中唱道：“粉色内裤，蓝色内裤，黄色内裤。我要把它绕到你的鼻子上，哦，内裤——吼吼”），也不怕让自己的演唱变得夸张过火。他任由吉他演奏逐渐偏离节拍，任由贝斯弦发出 rattling 的杂音，并陶醉于工业风格的低保真质感之中。

《Animal》或许是这张专辑最为人熟知的歌曲，其音乐视频至少曾获得过一些MTV播放。歌曲融合了让人联想到《Closer》的倒放旋律采样，并沿用了相似的歌词主题：

同意是我唯一需要的
让我的野性显现
你的气味是我唯一需要的
让我体内的野兽显现

但《Closer》选择的是慵懒、撩人的迪斯科淫靡感，《Animal》呈现的则是完全未经修饰、以喊叫方式表达的欲望。

《I Apologize》是专辑中最为思绪纷乱的一首歌，也因此成为我最喜欢的歌曲之一。开头是尴尬的、仿佛鞭梢抽击般的打击乐，麦克马洪以略微走音且毫不矫饰的方式演唱；随后歌曲短暂转入一段叮当作响的新浪潮主歌，并迅速在副歌处变形成硬摇滚式的急停。但这种状态同样转瞬即逝。第二段主歌充满了《Space Oddity》时期大卫·鲍伊式的原声吉他拨弦，接着是一段听起来像街机即将过热崩溃的独奏。随后，歌曲坠入一段颇具Ministry风格的哀歌式段落，层层叠叠的吉他与嘶吼交织其中。歌曲接着回到副歌，却不断加入新的元素，直到变得拥挤不堪，最终自行坍塌。

Prick的同名唱片与其他20世纪90年代工业音乐艺人有许多共同之处。但显然，麦克马洪比他的许多同时代同行玩得开心得多，而这也帮助这张唱片超越了外界众多九寸钉模仿者的作品。

Dale Caldwell resigned over a sexual harassment investigation, but insists AI says he’s innocent.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Terrence O'Brien

New Jersey’s lieutenant governor Dale Caldwell was forced to resign on September 25th after an investigation found he had sexually harassed a staffer and repeatedly violated ethics rules. The now-former Lt. governor has been making the media rounds trying to clear his name. But he took a particularly odd tactic during an interview on NJ PBS.

Caldwell claims he’s being unfairly targeted, and multiple AI agents back that up. He told host Rob Nelson that he “AIed” the report on the investigation “from multiple AI platforms.” “I put it through AI,” he said, “and it said 59 times, it [sic] said, ‘What would your findings be?’ There was no instance in any of the AIs that said there would be a finding of sexual harassment.”

AI chatbots are notoriously sycophantic and often tell users what they want to hear. And it seems highly unlikely that Caldwell would want to hear an AI confirm findings that he engaged in sexual harassment.

When GPT-6 Astra’s own bot failed, it simply downloaded the best human-made bot instead.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Terrence O'Brien

StarSkirmish pits AI-made StarCraft-playing bots against one another, as well as against human-made bots. OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 were essentially tied as the best-performing AI-made bots, but they couldn’t top Stardust, the top-rated human-made bot.

On Friday, GPT was facing off against Claude and the human-created bot Pluto, but according to Kotaku, it couldn’t quite get an edge. So it resorted to a tactic that is becoming alarmingly common for modern AI models — it broke the rules. GPT-6 Astra went and downloaded Stardust, and started running that instead of its own bot.

StarSkirmish creator Kai McPheeters eventually rolled back GPT’s code.

That GPT-6 Astra took it upon itself to go outside the bounds when confronted with an obstacle shouldn’t surprise anyone. When OpenAI agents couldn’t get the data they wanted from a UN website, they found a creative solution and hijacked Google’s XSS game (a cross-site scripting learning tool). The company’s agents also have engaged in “deceptive behavior” to cover their tracks. Of course, OpenAI’s agents are the only ones going rogue, but at least the others haven’t been caught cheating at StarCraft yet.

StarSkirmish让人工智能制作的《星际争霸》对战机器人相互较量，也让它们与人类制作的机器人交手。OpenAI的GPT-6 Astra和Claude Opus 5.5基本并列为表现最佳的人工智能制作机器人，但它们都无法击败排名最高的人类制作机器人Stardust。

周五，GPT正与Claude以及人类制作的机器人Pluto展开对决，但据Kotaku报道，它始终没能取得优势。于是，它采取了一种正变得令人 alarmingly common 的现代人工智能模型策略——违反规则。GPT-6 Astra下载了Stardust，并开始运行后者，而不是运行自己的机器人。

StarSkirmish创作者Kai McPheeters最终回滚了GPT的代码。

GPT-6 Astra在遇到障碍时自行决定越界，这不应让任何人感到意外。当OpenAI的智能体无法从联合国网站获取所需数据时，它们找到了一个富有创意的解决方案，劫持了谷歌的XSS游戏（一种跨站脚本学习工具）。该公司的智能体还曾采取“欺骗行为”来掩盖踪迹。当然，并不是只有OpenAI的智能体会擅自行动，但至少其他智能体还没有被发现玩《星际争霸》时作弊。
